evidence: The solution writes "Dividing (ii) by (i): \(\dfrac{x-h}{x} = \dfrac{\cot(\alpha-\beta)}{\cot\alpha}\)... rather, equating the two expressions for \(d\): ...". That ratio is INVERTED: from \(x\cot\alpha = (x-h)\cot(\alpha-\beta)\) the correct consequence is \(\dfrac{x-h}{x} = \dfrac{\cot\alpha}{\cot(\alpha-\beta)}\). Checked numerically at \(\alpha=60^\circ, \beta=20^\circ, h=10\): \((x-h)/x = 0.4845\), which equals \(\cot\alpha/\cot(\alpha-\beta)=0.4845\), NOT the printed \(\cot(\alpha-\beta)/\cot\alpha=2.064\). The final answer is right because the wrong line is abandoned mid-sentence ("... rather,") and the derivation restarts — but a student reads a false identity followed by visible failed scratch work in a printed answer key.
proposedFix: Delete the abandoned clause entirely and go straight from (i) and (ii) to the equality: "Equating the two expressions for \(d\): \(x\cot\alpha = (x-h)\cot(\alpha-\beta)\), so \(x[\cot(\alpha-\beta)-\cot\alpha] = h\cot(\alpha-\beta)\), giving \(x = \dfrac{h\cot(\alpha-\beta)}{\cot(\alpha-\beta)-\cot\alpha}\)." (Optionally add the one line that justifies step (ii): the elevation \(\alpha\) of the minar top from the tower foot equals the depression of the tower foot from the minar top, so the tower top sits at depression \(\alpha-\beta\).)

evidence: The solution ends "(The printed option C reverses the sign; the intended value is \(\dfrac{3-\sqrt{3}}{2}\).)" — but printed option C IS \(\dfrac{3-\sqrt{3}}{2}\), byte-for-byte the value the note claims is missing. The derivation itself is correct (\(h = \sqrt{3}/(\sqrt{3}+1) = (3-\sqrt{3})/2 \approx 0.6340\), verified numerically). The note appears to be a stale erratum from a version where option C read \((\sqrt{3}-3)/2\); as it stands it tells a student the option they are being asked to select is misprinted, when it is not.
proposedFix: Delete the parenthetical sentence. The solution should end: "... \(= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}-1)}{(\sqrt{3}+1)(\sqrt{3}-1)} = \dfrac{3-\sqrt{3}}{2}\) metres. Hence (C)."
